reviews.text: 游戏比较有趣的设计是新角色的解锁，所有敌方单位都是可以使用的，而解锁方式则是被敌方击杀。初始角色是一个幽灵，技能组我不是很喜欢，就我目前解锁的三个地狱角色来看，小丑的技能组里实用的被动不少，有攻击有概率获得道具，最高低于70%血量提高全属性，暴击后提高下一回合攻击的暴击几率，以及高达75%概率复活的被动。主打被动效果的话蓝量就省下来了，那么有一个带主动回血技能的肩甲就成了不让蓝量浪费的好东西，这个玩法基本就是无脑A，残血了可以走位拉扯一下拖技能CD，感觉挺有搞头的

This game checks all the boxes that it describes itself as. Creature collection but the creatures are basically angels and demons that you play as. Its a traditional Roguelike, no upgrades between runs except for new playable characters and a starting loot chest with a potion and random gear. When you lose a run your soul takes over the creature that killed you and you can now play as that creature which is very fun and unique. The dungeons are random but not random enough to know it is. Same enemies spawn on specific floors, layout is too similar to realize its different. Loot you get can be transmuted for XP and SP(skill points) which is basically mana to use skills. The game so far is very difficult and dying means starting all over from floor 1 with no reward to take back with you except for a new character. Plenty of characters to unlock, 52 in total. but not a huge amount of skills/passives. Theres basically no tutorial and on top of that you can't even see a description for a lot of items like certain potions or scrolls. It's very frustrating trying to figure some of this stuff out and even after using an item i couldn't tell what it did. Don't get me started on stats, theres a 12 different stats and trying to make a build is close to impossible because items increase stats and lower others at the same time, same as leveling up and choosing stat increases. want more Crit and HP? well we gotta lower your attack in exchange. The RNG of choosing a character, getting items that buff stats you need, as well as finding the right stat spread to make it work is just bad design for such a punishing game. Oh before i forget, your run can be ended by falling in a hole and there is early game enemies who can just push or pull you into one from long range. Despite all this and the game being in EA i would recommend it to those who like a good tactical game with roguelike element added but not for this price tag. in it's current state i would say its worth about $10. im going to keep playing because I enjoy it so far and update this reveiw with any new findings.
说是战棋，严格遵守回合制的对战，虽然战斗限制很大，但游戏意外的好玩，尤其夺舍的玩法，更是增加了游戏可玩性，而且人物角色也多，整体还是不错的

游戏有一个相当有意思的机制啊，就是你在局内被某个怪物打死后，你的灵魂就会附身到那个怪物身上，这样下次开局时你就能控制那个怪物作为你的闯关角色了，而且每个怪物都有各种不同的技能，就感觉像是一种另类的宝可梦收集方式啊。开荒思路就是要你在局内尽量去找到那种更厉害更高级的怪物，并且死亡夺舍它，这样你下次开局用它去闯关就算是有提升了。亮点在于可以夺舍敌人，用敌人的属性来进行下一盘游戏，你才能走的更远，代替了常见的局外成长，很有创意，也就是说随着你深入地牢，遇到更强的敌人，击败它，解锁它， 夺舍它，成为它，用它的属性继续闯关，解锁更猛的角色，继续循环，可以，很有创意很NICE~
上班摸鱼就决定是它了哈哈哈哈哈
挺有创意的肉鸽刷宝游戏。夺舍规则与半即时回合制玩法赋予了游戏更加深度的策略意义…… 开局只有一个“灵魂”，可以选择天堂或地狱场景进入~ 推荐开局两个门都进一下，多死几次，利用游戏的“夺舍”规则开局就获取几个新角色~ 每个角色都有不同的装备栏、技能和特点~选择一个适合自己的再去闯关…… 如果途中遇到新的喜欢的角色也可以“战略性死亡”让它把你干掉~再选取这个更加强大的角色重新开始……
每个怪都是一个职业，看似玩法丰富，但实际是通用技能的排列组合，很少有独特职业机制。熟悉了技能后每个职业玩法可以一眼看到头。 到了高层之后堆怪且数值非常不平衡，装备给的还和低层一样。玩家升级完全跟不上怪变强的速度。 在低层熟悉游戏的时候还挺有趣的，之后玩的一肚子火。在开发者大规模调整数值平衡之前不推荐游玩。

玩法类似于《风来的西林》系列的地牢肉鸽探索，战斗方式为回合制，每当我方移动、攻击、使用道具的同时，敌人也会同步采取行动。在1v1的时候可以凭硬实力战斗，但是面对多个敌人就会很吃力，正确的策略是引导敌人触发地形中的机关和陷阱，借此来缓解压力。另外，本作有一个比较有意思的夺舍系统，当我们被某个敌人干掉后能获得对应的能力，不断地死在各种敌人手中也成了游戏必经的一环。不过二层开始敌人就变得很强了，希望后续数值能再平衡调整一下
俯视角3D地牢肉鸽探索游戏，一开始我以为是完全的即时战斗类型，直到怪物追着我，我走一格它走一格时，我才发现事情并没有我想象的那么简单；游戏现在的数值存在着一定的问题，所以在战斗体验之中难免会有些吃力，不过运用好策略还是有着一战之力的；另外，这个天使瞪着两个大眼睛实在是有些过于呆萌了，哈哈哈哈哈！
目前能玩，但一则缺少局外成长极其容易开局暴毙，二则哪怕到了高层也没有高级独特装备，三则技能树太浅还无藏品，还不太行，但底子和创意很不错，ea阶段多拓展内容倒也有可能成为佳作。

游戏UI界面满满的复古感，过场动画有点太过简陋了作为一款肉鸽探索游戏，战斗为回合制，指引方面并没有做出很好的引导（伙计们战斗之前记得先把装备穿戴上），升级后可提升属性，主要分为2大派系罪孽与美德， 美德为：贞洁、节制、勤勉、耐心、仁慈、谦逊、慈善7项，罪孽为色欲、暴食、懒惰、暴怒、嫉妒、傲慢、贪婪7项，加点后会有2项增益和1项负面增益，如色欲效果（暴击率+、暴击伤害+ 治疗量-） 耐心效果（最大生命值+ 暴击率+ 速度-），分支选项略有不同，请谨慎选择。不用的装备可以转化，转化成功可以获得经验值和灵力，失败会扣除灵力。很多装备都自带属性，如暴怒护腿、贪婪护腿，就会增加相应的属性。游戏中独特的夺舍复苏能力是游戏的核心特色，被敌人杀死会占据他的身体，活的他的能力来以牙还牙，游戏体验之后，打的不是很爽，数值上不够合理，ui 地图 环境 特效都需要再加打磨，另外游戏鼠标和键盘不能够同时操作，希望能及时更新改善。

这是一款回合制策略战棋游戏。 游戏的画面是3D建模，但是建模水平一般，基本就是十年前的水准，而且虽然是说是天使和恶魔两大阵营，但敌人看着都和恶魔似的，不太好看。技能特效和效果也不够花哨，总体来说游戏画面比较落后。 优化还行，不过就这建模水平如果还有卡顿那也太过分了。 背景说的是玩家死后扮演的魂灵遇到了天使和恶魔，恶魔还奚落主角如果是好人应该上天堂才对，来到这肯定不是好人。然后天使开始劝说主角去地狱杀点恶魔，恶魔则让主角去天堂干掉那些虚伪的天堂生物，然后玩家就可以任选一个传送门开始游戏了。 玩法上是回合制战棋，不过是那种按照敌我速度排序的那种，如果玩家速度属性够高，那就能够多次行动，而玩家行动回合之后敌人也会立刻行动。 地图基本上可以理解成就两张，就是天堂和地狱，选择了天堂地图，那么这一路上地图都是天堂风格，完全没啥变化，选地狱也是如此。 玩家要做的就是在地图里找寻上楼的楼梯，直到通关或者死亡。 流程中遇到敌人就开始战斗，地图上有着各种陷阱，玩家可以使用普攻或者技能来和敌人战斗，同时可以考虑用技能把敌人拉入陷阱什么的，稍微有一些策略性。 当然在你觉得你能把敌人推到坑里秒杀敌人的时候请注意，敌人也能把你拉到坑里让你直接重来。 打死敌人之后可以获得装备和经验，升级之后能够点属性并升级技能。 属性的设置选择任意一个升级都能提高两个属性并降低另一个，比如点勤勉，那么就会增加暴击伤害和速度，但是会降低攻击力，所以在加属性的时候是需要一定抉择的。 装备也会增加或者减少某些属性，装备的时候也需要计较一下。 游戏有特色的地方在于，玩家如果被敌人打死，那么玩家就会失去全部的装备和属性，然后能在下局玩杀死你的这个角色。而这个角色的技能和属性偏向都会和别的角色略有区别。 不过由于没有局外成长，所以把这个当成收集宝可梦当成核心玩法就不太行了，玩个一两次就会觉得很单调。 有中文。 总体来说是个很old school的游戏，如果是二十年前玩到这个我大概会觉得很好玩，但是这个年代了，还是这种复古的玩法就很无趣了。 价格对比玩法算是很贵了，仅推荐钱多烧包的玩家购买。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] 遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url] 点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

This game has a lot of potential, but I cannot recommend it at its current stage. The design where you unlock the monster that killed you as a playable character is very interesting. However, the game's main problem right now is that while the character roster appears large, it suffers from severe homogenization, making the roguelike experience highly repetitive. The monsters' skill trees are too similar to each other. While some monsters have skills designed for synergy, the actual gameplay experience with them is very clunky and unsatisfying. Other issues include monotonous map design, a lack of random events, and a high degree of repetition in the skills provided by equipment.
制作人玩过自己的游戏吗？ 怪物多一层数值就暴增，玩家一层，全是垃圾装备，三四点攻击力还要减命中减防御，垃圾药剂，飞行免疫隐身。 玩家清完一层数值都不够，还敢跳怪去刷数值更高的？结果清完了下一层，还是被数值、数量碾压。 打了几个小时了，再打几个小时，我想不出除了多解锁几个怪还能有什么提升。

玩了两天就一把走到第六层，这怪每层血多出接近一百点，攻击加十点，我把一层的怪全杀了也升不了两级，升一级三个点，这游戏属性点点了全有副作用，基本上你点了攻击就没血量，点了血量就没攻击，点了暴击扣闪避点了闪避扣防御，点满了属性还没小怪高，到第六层直接好家伙，一个一千八血的狼人加两个八百血的小怪，攻击都六十点，进去强制一打三，那小怪面板都比我高，我玩的又不是魂游，目前不知道怎么赢，感觉得加给局外成长，角色差距太大了
现阶段游玩性不高，高难度同时低反馈，哪怕一直sl刷到高等级，基本也没什么作用，该死还得死。
不要买，不要买，不要买根本不完善，你正常玩都打不过第3层，怪的数值太高，你的数值太低

[h1] 《弑神者的战棋》：天堂与地狱皆无人能敌 [/h1] 当人死后会变成什么样子了？有的人会说是灵魂，有的人会说直接没了，但我万万没想到这款《弑神者的战棋》在游戏里面用文本说出人死后会变成泥一样的存在，当然这也一定程度上的代表了灵魂的可塑性，算是后面各种形态一个还算合理的解释吧。 当然游戏整体玩法还算是不错，体验来说难度也不算高，目标也很简单就是杀穿地狱或者是杀穿天堂，虽然眼前站着一个天使一个恶魔都互相让我们干掉对面hhh [h3] 走格子战棋玩法，搭配万千变化 [/h3] 游戏的主要玩法就是通过格子战棋的方式，玩家们在不同房间里面探索，会搜集到一些武器资源，像什么木棍，宝剑，小红瓶和小蓝瓶，那个小黄瓶的曼德拉药我倒是没用过不清楚是干嘛的因为游戏里面也没有个明显的道具介绍啊喂！不过我个人还是喜欢积累红瓶，大不了没蓝了就平A比谁血多嘛，但需要注意的是我们背包数量上是有限的 而游戏中的战斗交互上来说其实就是经典的你一下，我一下玩法，玩家们可以使用不同的技能应但大部分的战斗体验来说都是互相平A，当然一些角色可以选择边走边打的方式，例如靠着走位放夹子，然后夹子本身有两回合冷却，加上每回合都只能够一动的机制其实1v1情况下大多数时候都会处于不败之地，不过真的大部分情况都只有一个敌人单对单么？ 而游戏里面也有着养成玩法，前面提到的局内装备系统就是一点，还有着对应的技能天赋树（我其实感觉是图标做的比较大所以看起来多hhh）和基础的属性加点这两种，不过挨着清图点的话还是挺快的，而且装备道具还可以去赌一波运气强化，但是概率实际体验下来也是相当的感人QAQ 而最重要的一点就是游戏的角色，这里的话叫作换了一个形态。游戏里面可以通过我们不断的挑战来解锁更多的角色，每一个角色都有着不同的技能和形态，也算是让我们在同质化游戏内容上面减少重复感，数量上是真的挺多的。 [h3] 总结 [/h3] 作为一款轻松向的战棋游戏来说，游戏本身的可玩性还是非常高的毕竟多样化的技能树，大量的属性加点外带丰富的角色数量，至少体量这块是完全没得问题的，如果对于这种回合制战棋游戏感兴趣的小伙伴，可以尝试体验一下。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45519015/]“无趣评测”[/url][/td][/table]

[h1]一念踏平天堂，一念横扫地狱[/h1] 在《弑神者的战棋》里我们是一个不死不灭的灵魂体，生前应该是一个令神魔都颤抖的人物，如今变成了灵魂体依然能引来所罗门72柱魔神排行29的阿斯塔罗斯和西方堕天使“月之天使”沙利叶的争抢，希望我们能为他们而征战！而我们的选择？小孩子才做选择，“大人物”当然是全都要！所以我们就从此成了一边打天堂，一边揍地狱的不死战士了！ 游戏是3D立体构筑，虽说某些场景的视角转动起来还是较为别扭，但最起码地狱有着地狱的样子，各种陷阱和装饰也都有那么几分昏暗堕落的味道；而天堂则是富丽堂皇充满神圣的光芒。一个独立战棋游戏能做到这程度也已经算是相当不错了。 游戏的战斗采用了较为简单的战棋机制，虽说平时的活动也是“走格子”的模式，但一旦遇敌就会进入你一下我一下的回合制战棋。角色的速度属性会影响我们的出手频率，速度越快，出手越多。而且场景地形也会能被利用起来，比如使用头槌一类的推动技能把敌人推入陷阱就是个很不错的以弱胜强的方法！遇到一些不可战胜的或者被以多欺少了，也只有地形陷阱能给我们一线生机的。 《弑神者的战棋》最大的特色就是他新颖的“夺舍”机制，游戏里我们只要被干掉就能获得对方的资料，从而在从头再来的时候就能以“它”的形态和能力去战斗！就连技能天赋树和成长表都是独特的，这也就是说所有与我们为敌，无论他多么强大，终究都会是我们“养成”的目标！而且能成长的我们只会变得比它们更强！ 游戏目前有着天堂和地狱俩个阵营共51位角色（加上初始的灵魂体是52位）供我们解锁选择，这个阵营也已经算庞大了，不过各个角色哪怕都是1级起始，却也都有着强弱之分，毕竟大恶魔和大天使的战力，哪怕是1级也不是一个地狱小鬼可以比拟的嘛！因此在遇到高级角色的时候千万不要犹豫，果断死在它手上将是我们愉快游戏的不二法门！ 游戏的装备系统也是游戏一个较为重要的一个玩法，虽说目前装备系统还是较为粗糙，高等阶的比低等阶的只是数值上的差距而已，但毕竟还在EA阶段，后续如果给装备添加各种技能加成之类的属性，或者套装系统什么的，应该可以让装备系统更好玩才是的。 整体而言，《弑神者的战棋》应该是想用最简单的战棋机制融合最新颖的“夺舍”玩法来唤起我们对战棋游戏的希望和念想了。只要再细细打磨，应该是可以成功的才是！ [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45145702//]左邻右里鉴赏组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 游戏好不好玩，只有玩过才知道！ [/b][/u]

[h1][b]以彼之道还施彼身，能夺舍的肉鸽战棋[/b][/h1] 《弑神者的战棋》是一款非常特别的半即时制回合策略游戏，玩家扮演一名误入混沌之地的灵魂，将辗转于天堂和地狱，用夺舍转生之力一次次冒险，探寻整个世界的真相。 游戏的开场是一段天使和恶魔的口头交锋，二者及尽可能的引导主角前往另一方领地去战斗。 接下来便是玩家的选择了，左侧为地狱之门，进入之后一片昏暗，到处都是滚烫的岩浆，右侧为天堂之门，这里富丽堂皇，但仍有重兵把守。 两个世界均分为了多层，玩家需要逐步探索场景，打怪升级提升实力，寻找出口进入更深的层级。 本作不同于以往关卡制的战棋，游戏如同Rogue游戏一样会随机生成地图，每一层都会分为若干个房间，进入新的房间敌人便会开始袭击，双方将在格子战场上展开对决。 直接点击敌人可施展普通攻击，点击左下角的技能图标或是按下数字键也可释放对应的技能，不同的技能覆盖范围也不同，诸如打击前方三格、周遭八格、前后左右四格等，其中一些技能附带击退效果，利用好这个特性将敌人击退到陷阱或者墙上可以造成额外伤害。 游戏还加入了装备和升级加点系统，装备可经由游戏前的箱子、杀敌掉落、场景探索等途径获得。 部分装备拥有特殊效果，如降低被敌人被刺的伤害、被弹幕击中后获得额外回合等，另外一些装备还会附带额外的技能，带来战略意义上的提升。 本作的最大亮点是夺舍玩法，当角色死亡后，击杀者将会转变为可用角色，且是永久解锁。 游戏为每个角色都做了单独的设计，包含基础属性、角色特性、技能树等内容，这个玩法非常有意思，其促使玩家不断了解敌人组成，这样下次战斗将能更加得心应手，当然玩家也可以利用这一机制，故意让特定敌人将自己杀死，从而解锁其角色。 整体来说是非常有意思的一款游戏，虽然操作和传统战棋差不多，但玩法完全不一样，大场景探索+装备系统+升级系统+夺舍玩法这一套组合颇具新意，不断熟悉每个角色的过程也充满了乐趣。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]

《弑神者的战棋》是由Nine Dots Studio制作的一款回合制战棋游戏，你将扮演一个不死不灭的灵魂体，在天堂与地狱的废墟中展开冒险。游戏最大的特色就是独特的"夺舍"机制，让死亡变成了获得力量的机会。 [h2]死亡不是终点[/h2] 这游戏最有意思的地方就是"夺舍"系统了~当你被敌人击败后，不仅不会真正死亡，反而能夺取对方的躯壳和能力！这意味着每个曾经击败你的敌人，最终都会成为你可以使用的角色。游戏里有52个不同的角色可以解锁，从小恶魔到大天使应有尽有，每个角色的技能和玩法都完全不同。 有时候遇到强敌，故意"送死"反而是最聪明的选择，因为获得它的能力后你就能以更强的姿态重新挑战！这种设计让失败也变得有意义。 [h2]经典战棋玩法[/h2] 游戏采用走格子的战棋模式，你需要在随机生成的地牢房间中探索。平时可以自由移动，但靠近敌人就会进入回合制战斗。地形和陷阱的利用也很重要，比如用头槌把敌人推进岩浆，或者巧妙走位让敌人互相伤害。 装备系统虽然比较简单，但配合不同角色的专属装备栏，还是能搭配出不少有趣的组合。技能树的设计也挺特别，通常是提升某方面能力的同时会降低另一方面，所以加点需要考虑清楚。 [h2]总体感受[/h2] 作为一款独立战棋游戏，《弑神者的战棋》的创意和可玩性都挺不错的。夺舍机制让每次失败都有收获，52个角色保证了足够的重复游玩价值。虽然某些系统还比较粗糙，但整体体验还是蛮有趣的。 如果你喜欢战棋类游戏，或者对这种"越死越强"的设定感兴趣，可以尝试一下~ [quote]关注：「[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45549554/]慕之安鉴赏组」[/url]，慕赏游韵，安品游情[/quote] [u][b]“慕之安鉴赏组”静候同路人。[/b][/u]

Lost in Prayer is my first traditional roguelike. I wasn't sure if I'd like the grid based gameplay as I worried it would take the fun out of a good build due to being slower and (sort of) turn based. The game hooked me, however, and it's absolutely fantastic. It is difficult as you're beginning and learning the mechanics, and then as you familiarize yourself with them it becomes manageable. Mistakes will still lead to failure VERY FAST though (I just had what felt like a god run end due to me being a dummy and not thinking things through). Unlocking new characters by dying to them is very cool and added a lot to the early game. It really made me think on what I valued more when I was in the middle of a really good run - did I want to push through and try to succeed in the run, or did I want to die to the cool-looking new enemy so I could play as them? The only downside is that there is a finite amount of characters, so this loop does come to an end eventually (looking forward to more being added throughout early access though). And characters play very different from each other which is awesome. The game in its current state does not explain much and forces you to deduce or learn through trial and error. This goes for things like how stat upgrades scale, how characters are meant to be played, and even what effect different potions give you. To be clear, this is not a negative - figuring these things out, such as unlocking a new character and spending a little time trying to understand how their kit functions before playing them for the first time, was a ton of fun. All in all, I would highly recommend this game to anybody who is even remotely interested. And the "endgame" of trying to clear both Heaven and Hell with each character is addicting, as the types of builds to make different characters viable are very diverse and interesting.

Note that Lost in Prayer at the time of this review is in early access, and I have a personal bias towards ninedots because of my love for Outward. I enjoy this game enough to recommend it to fans of rather difficult roguelikes. The most recent update was pretty major and completely rebalanced the game, so I'm confident that the gameplay will continue to grow and change on its way to 1.0. This however also means I can't effectively predict how the game will play by then. There are a lot of interesting concepts here: You control a soul stuck in purgatory and the only way out is to conquer EITHER Heaven or Hell. You are given the options of two completely different dungeon paths to take that have wildly different enemies and hazards. I personally find the Hell route a bit easier than Heaven so I tend to go there for most of my runs. Whenever you are killed by an enemy in Lost in Prayer, you unlock that enemy to play as on future runs. This is a fun incentive to death, and when I know a run is cooked, I will beeline for the toughest looking new enemy and get them to kill me so I can try a new character. There are also unique, really powerful characters that you kind of "secretly" unlock by dying to floor hazards. You will still certainly die more than you will unlock new content from it, but it plays a part in exploring further into the dungeon in a neat way. The turn-based combat of the game is very strategic due to the INSANELY TIGHT action economy. You may spend exactly one action on your turn: attack, use a skill, MOVE ONE SPACE, or use a potion. It's quite the learning curve getting over moving exactly one space ending your turn. To combat this, the speed stat may eventually let you take two turns in a row, as well as there are skills that slow enemies or (now since the most recent update) skills that simply give you an extra turn when you use them. Characters without this bonus to action economy typically have skills that combine moving and attacking, or skills they active that automatically move them when certain conditions are met. I'm gonna be honest, it took my probaby 5 of my 12 hours so far to get over how much I HATED the action economy. Now I value it as part of the unique experience this roguelike provides and enjoy learning new ways around it. The levelling system is cute at first, but ultimately needs some paring down imo. You gain experience fighting monsters to level up, but the xp curve for levelling seems to be more exponential than the number of enemies I seem to encounter. To combat this, every item you pick up can be scrapped for a percentage chance you give you varying levels of xp rewards and other potential buffs. If you get lucky, exactly one piece of starting gear you might not like could give you enough xp to level up before you even start your run. If you get horribly unlucky, scrapping every item you aren't using won't grant you nearly enough xp to remain in line with the difficulty of dungeon floors. Now, they've added a pseudo trader entity to some dungeon floors that you can exchange gear with, but for the most part your unwanted gear's primary purpose is to become more XP. I personally don't think this should be as random as it is now, or that enemies should give more XP. Gear drops can be pretty decent from time to time, but ultimatley without the XP to level up, you'll be toast quick. It's not a risk/reward balance, you're just expected to break old stuff and get something out of it as part of progression and bad RNG can absolutely hose you. On top of that, you are given 3 points each level to invest in any of the 7 heavenly virtues and/or deadly sins. It's cute flavor and on-theme, but ultimately means you have FOURTEEN Attributes to choose from every time you level up. To make it more complicated, each attribute raises 2 stats and lowers another. One may raise your attack and accuracy, but lower your defense. No problem, you say to yourself, you'll just take two attributes that raise defense to avoid the drop. Uh oh, that stat raises you defense and special attack, but lowers your accuracy! Maybe your character has a high starting accuracy and that's not a problem? Oh, also each piece of gear you find is linked to one of the FOURTEEN (14 [10 + 4 = too many]) attributes, which will then raise and lower these attributes as you get new pieces of armor or weapons. So you spend your level up increasing your attack and accuracy, but then all the armor you find undoes those stat raises, and you really need the passive skills they give or the defense bonuses. That's actually one thing I will say you can kind of breathe on: better gear always raises defense more, and better weapons will increase attack and/or special more. So you can try to balance your levelling choices by accepting little hits to attack/defense here and there, knowing every piece of armor will correct for that. I don't think the sin/virtue system is bad, I just think its wildly complex for a roguelike. I've spent more time thinking about building out my stats than it takes to clear the first floor of the dungeon. These runs aren't long, and none of these stats carry over to future runs. I just think the system should be more streamlined. Fourteen attributes that raise and lower stats, are linked to every piece of gear AND (almost forgot to mention) each enemy has specific strengths and weaknesses to just make the stat boosting complicated at best and arbitrary at worst. All that being said, the game feels pretty polished, and mechanics feel intentional. The big update it just received shows me the devs aren't sold on balance yet and are also willing to make big sweeping changes if it's potentially for the better. Like I said, I'll buy anything ninedots does thanks to Outward, but I do legitimately think Lost in Prayer can be worth the price to a fan of roguelikes looking for something different, with a LOOOOOOT (too much?) of versitality

Lost in Prayer is, on the whole, a good game. The unique twist - playing as your killer - is complimented well by a generous roster of interesting creatures with reasonably varied skill trees. Nine Dots is an innovative and uncompromising developer. I would recommend the game at full price as an investment in the full potential of LiP. Currently there's plenty to play around with. Over 20 playable creatures, several viable playstyles, and some interesting loot to uncover. But there are areas of the game left wanting. The story, design of the levels and variability of items all have room to grow. Over all, in its current state, LiP still manages to be lots of fun. Future updates will really push this game from the 'good' to 'great' category. I have full confidence in Nine Dots to deliver. I kept it too long under my wishlist. Game loop is very fun and even kind of new, considering it's not a normal "monster capture" type of mechanic which is the core of the loop. Reminds me of how fun Dungeons of Dredmor was, a fresh experience just like this one. I specially loved the many references to Outward (a masterpiece btw, highly recommended). The many builds and choices are great. There are even some "brainless" builds, which I enjoy a lot. Graphics are OK, visual style is "hit-or-miss" (if you loved the styiling in Outward it might suit you yoo!), performance is Good, soundtrack is Good too. Get the game if you enjoy fast roguelikes and gameplay loops.

Lost in Prayer is super interesting. It blends old school 90s roguelike gameplay with modern 3D graphics and art style. The concept of being able to play as a character that's defeated you opens up a lot of fun decisions about how exactly you want your run to end. Being able to take a demon that slayed you into the heavenly realm and vice versa also offers some neat gameplay decisions.
The core idea is brilliant: if you’re defeated, your next run can start as the very monster that defeated you. Genius, right?
Made by a Canadian Studio ❤️
